Follows from the nivolumab role decision below.

Conditions list 'High Grade Glioma (III or IV)': grade 4 explicitly allowed, no IDH requirement, glioblastoma never named, which D30-R7 includes as historical glioblastoma (mixed_glioma_gbm_named). Eligibility itself says only 'imaging of highly suspicious high grade glioma (HGG)', so the grade appears only in a condition term.

All registered outcomes concern nivo800 'as a molecular imaging agent' and the nivo800 dose 'in a total dose of 240 mg (nivolumab + nivo800 = 240 mg)'; no antitumour hypothesis or outcome is registered for unlabelled nivolumab.

Unlabelled nivolumab is given as a single infusion 'keeping the overall dose nivolumab + nivo800 no more than 240 mg' before SOC resection, i.e. to make the tracer reflect a therapeutic dose for imaging (rule 0b, used only for diagnosis); no antitumour outcome is registered. A therapeutic reading is possible because patients receive a full checkpoint-inhibitor dose and the summary cites nivolumab's promise in HGG.
